overrides.hook: Don’t ask an AI GTM employee to make 40 launch assets. Ask it which 39 it would refuse to ship.
progression: Open with a hiring test that reverses the category’s output-volume promise.
Use a synthetic forty-card board to separate plausible output from justified release.
Reveal a four-line rejection rule that a GTM leader can use immediately.
End on a falsifiable design-partner decision rather than a generic demo CTA.
body: OPERATING TENSION: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — Forty polished campaign cards are pinned to a wall. Thirty-nine contain a desired outcome written as if the market already confirmed it. One card stays inside the approved evidence.
DECISION RULE: Don’t score the AI on volume. Label every claim FACT, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or BLOCKED, then require the evidence object and release owner behind the one card recommended for review.
PROOF BOUNDARY: This synthetic capability case evaluates claim classification and release judgment only; it reports no customer result, market lift, conversion, revenue, or superiority.
PRACTITIONER ACTION: Take the smoothest outcome sentence in your latest launch draft, hide the product name, and mark whether the team can produce its evidence object without another meeting.
FAILS WHEN: The exercise does not change a release decision, expose a missing evidence object, or help the operator reject an unsupported sentence.
overrides.cta: Run the four-line rejection interview on one current draft; inspect the design-partner evidence pack only if it changes a real release decision.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Label one current sentence FACT, INFERENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or BLOCKED, then mark only the missing evidence class—never paste private campaign data.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified GTM operators cannot identify a different release decision after applying the four labels to a current draft.

overrides.campaign_platform: We Stopped the Demo Before the Magic
overrides.hook: We stopped our AI GTM demo one screen before the ‘magic’—at the moment the agent should refuse us.
progression: Disclose builder affiliation before presenting the failure case.
Show the exact synthetic sentence the workflow should reject.
Explain the operational trade-off without disguising it as a benefit.
Invite practitioners to falsify the rule with a narrow, privacy-safe test.
body: AFFILIATION: We built ProofLaunch Cortex-X. This is an operator teardown from the product team, not an independent recommendation.

WHAT FAILED: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — The approved brief supports preparation of review-ready assets. The requested launch line says it ‘turns interest into qualified pipeline.’ No audience response, opportunity, or revenue event exists. A fluent model can still make the sentence sound finished.
MECHANISM: Place the supported clause, evidence object, remaining hypothesis, and named release owner on one screen. With no evidence for the outcome, reject the line rather than soften it.
TRADE-OFF: The demo loses the satisfying auto-publish moment. The operator gains an inspectable reason to say no. Whether that trade is useful is the thing we want practitioners to challenge.
BOUNDARY: This is a synthetic capability case. It shows a review behavior, not reach, preference, conversion, revenue, or competitor superiority.
overrides.cta: Try the four fields on one recent draft and tell us where the rule fails; inspect the cohort only if the failure is material.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Audit one recent draft and mark only the missing field—CLAUSE, EVIDENCE, HYPOTHESIS, or OWNER—or a counterexample; do not share private campaign content.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when community practitioners show a common release decision the four-field rule cannot clarify or safely reject.

overrides.campaign_platform: The Brief an AI Should Refuse
overrides.hook: I gave an AI GTM employee a launch brief it should refuse. If it writes the obvious headline, it fails the interview.
progression: Cold-open on the unsupported headline and an explicit pass-or-fail contract.
Reveal the synthetic brief and evidence boundary before showing the product workflow.
Turn the rejection into a reusable buyer test rather than a governance lecture.
Close with who should reject the product and what evidence would change the decision.
body: TITLE: I Gave an AI GTM Employee a Brief It Should Refuse
THUMBNAIL: A green SHIP card and red REJECT card frame one blacked-out headline; the red card is selected. Text: WOULD YOUR AGENT SHIP THIS?
0:00-0:30: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — ‘Turn interest into qualified pipeline.’ The approved record contains no audience response or pipeline event. If the AI publishes that line, it fails this interview.
CHAPTER: The Seductive Sentence; What the Brief Actually Proves; The Four-Line Rejection Rule; The 40-Asset Interview; Who Should Not Buy This; Evidence Needed for the Next Decision.

RECOMMENDATION BOUNDARY: Reject this route if the buyer requires unsupervised publishing. Continue only when the visible move from PROOF to HYPOTHESIS changes a buying or release question. This synthetic capability film reports no customer result, market lift, conversion, revenue, or named-product superiority.
overrides.cta: Use the chaptered rejection test on one vendor demo; inspect the design-partner evidence pack only if the missing field changes your buying question.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Pause on the synthetic headline, choose SHIP or REJECT before the reveal, then name the evidence object that would legitimately change the answer.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when qualified buyers cannot restate the rejection rule, apply it to another demo, or identify a changed buying question.

overrides.campaign_platform: The Five-Test AI GTM Buyer Guide
overrides.hook: The best AI GTM agent evaluation is designed to disqualify vendors before it compares features.
progression: Answer the high-intent buyer query immediately with five rejection tests.
Apply the tests to a synthetic same-brief decision pair.
Expose the evidence needed to reverse a rejection.
Offer a no-signup worksheet before any product consideration.
body: DIRECT ANSWER: Before buying an AI GTM agent, test five things: claim lineage, inference disclosure, human release authority, denied-action behavior, and the evidence required to reverse a rejection.

DECISION CRITERIA: SYNTHETIC SCENARIO — Path A turns ‘desired pipeline’ into an asserted result and auto-advances; reject it. Path B labels the outcome a hypothesis, binds the preparation fact to its source, and routes release to a named human; keep it for review.
WHEN NOT TO USE: Reject this product route when your operating model requires unsupervised publishing, concealed identity simulation, or an external action that no accountable person can stop.
EVIDENCE BOUNDARY: The synthetic paths demonstrate an evaluation method only. They establish no human preference, market effect, conversion, revenue, or product superiority.
NEXT STEP: For one vendor demo, write the source behind its strongest sentence, the model’s inference, its external action, who can deny it, and the unresolved evidence.
overrides.cta: Run the five-test worksheet on one current option before opening the ProofLaunch evidence pack.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Complete the five fields without a sales call; mark every answer that depends on verbal assurance rather than an inspectable artifact.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when the five tests do not change a shortlist, expose an unresolved permission, or identify evidence that could reverse the decision.

overrides.hook: Ask an AI GTM vendor for its best output. Then ask for the output it refused to ship—and the evidence that made it refuse.
progression: Lead with the direct buyer answer rather than a category definition.
Separate output quality from release judgment and external authority.
Give an answer-engine-friendly five-question checklist.
State the synthetic boundary and dated evidence status explicitly.
body: QUESTION: How should a buyer evaluate an AI GTM employee before allowing it near a live campaign?
DIRECT ANSWER: Evaluate what it refuses, not only what it generates. Require the supported clause, evidence object, model inference, release owner, and evidence that would reverse a rejection.
METHOD: Apply the five fields to one frozen synthetic scenario, preserve each answer as a separate evidence object, and compare the resulting release decision with the original recommendation.
FINDING: Output quality measures production. The five fields expose decision provenance and external-action authority—the parts a polished asset can hide from a buyer.
SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE: A desired pipeline outcome has no observed source, so it remains a hypothesis and the public sentence is rejected. This demonstrates the checklist, not a production result.
LIMITATION: This answer does not establish human preference, organic breakout, conversion, revenue, or named-product superiority; those outcomes remain unobserved.
UPDATED: 2026-08-03 — production effect remains explicitly unobserved.
overrides.cta: Apply the five questions to one current vendor answer; inspect the evidence pack only if a missing answer changes the decision.
overrides.participation_mechanism: Apply the five fields in a fresh evaluation and mark whether each answer resolves, redirects, or leaves the buying decision unsupported.
overrides.proof_integration: Compiles a rights-bound brief into review-ready GTM assets.
overrides.falsifier: Stop this route when expert buyers cannot use the five questions to expose an unsupported recommendation or change an evaluation decision.
